faq.q: What Markdown features does the preview render?
faq.a: Headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, links, images, inline code and fenced code blocks, blockquotes, unordered/ordered lists, GitHub-style task lists with checkboxes, tables, and horizontal rules. The parser is self-contained (no external library) and escapes HTML first to stay XSS-safe. It renders live as you type in a split view.

faq.q: Are links in my document safe, or can they run scripts?
faq.a: The renderer only allows http(s), mailto, tel, relative and #anchor URLs. A link or image written with a javascript: URL is left as literal text rather than becoming clickable, so a shared .md file can't execute script when opened. Code spans are also stashed before formatting, so text like `snake_case` or `[a](b)` inside backticks stays literal.

faq.q: What toolbar buttons and shortcuts are available?
faq.a: Toolbar buttons insert bold, italic, strikethrough, H1–H3, link, image, inline code, code block, blockquote, bullet/numbered/task lists, a table template and a horizontal rule. Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+B for bold, Ctrl/Cmd+I for italic, Ctrl/Cmd+K for a link. A view toggle switches between Edit, Split and Preview.

faq.q: Can I export my work and is it saved automatically?
faq.a: Yes. You can copy the Markdown or the rendered HTML, download a .md file, export a standalone styled .html document, or print/save as PDF. A stats bar shows word count, character count, line count and an estimated reading time (~200 words/min). Your content autosaves to local storage under toolbox-md and is restored next visit; 'Clear' wipes it.
